newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Direct Capital takes stake in EFT-POS NZ.
newsitem.headline: Direct Capital takes stake in EFT-POS NZ.

text.p: Direct Capital said on Monday it had taken a stake in the electronic funds transfer business with a $7.4 million investment for a one third holding in EFT-POS NZ.
The company is a leading player in the provision, installation and service of EFTPOS terminals.
"Direct Capital's investment will provide the company with the balance sheet strength to take advantage of some very exciting future opportunities," said Direct Capital director Bill Kermode.
"We see this as not only an investment in the fastest-growing payment system in the world, but also a sign of our belief that EFT-POS NZ, specifically, is a company with tremendous potential."
Direct Capital has a philosophy of taking minority positions in unlisted medium sized businesses with growth potential.
Direct Capital said NZ has the highests penetration of EFTPOS terminals in the world, with a terminal for every 78 people.
It is estimated that $13.85 billion, or 32 percent of total retail sales, went through EFTPOS terminals in NZ last year - an increase of approximately 25 percent on the year before.
"Growth is continuing into new markets such as taxis, doctors, plumbers and other trades people, plus sports clubs," said Kermode.
